name: Trojan.Mebromi
description_en: Trojan.Mebromi is BIOS-level malware that takes control of the victim before MBR. [1]

name: Mimikatz
description_en: Mimikatz is a credential dumper capable of obtaining plaintext Windows account logins and passwords, along with many other features that make it useful for testing the security of networks. [1] [2]
summary_es: Herramienta capaz de extraer y examinar material de autenticación en sistemas Windows. También se utiliza en auditorías autorizadas; su presencia requiere contexto.

name: RIPTIDE
description_en: RIPTIDE is a proxy-aware backdoor used by APT12 . [1]

name: TinyZBot
description_en: TinyZBot is a bot written in C# that was developed by Cleaver . [1]

name: Windows Credential Editor
description_en: Windows Credential Editor is a password dumping tool. [1]

name: pwdump
description_en: pwdump is a credential dumper. [1]

name: Skeleton Key
description_en: Skeleton Key is malware used to inject false credentials into domain controllers with the intent of creating a backdoor password. [1] Functionality similar to Skeleton Key is included as a module in Mimikatz .

name: gsecdump
description_en: gsecdump is a publicly-available credential dumper used to obtain password hashes and LSA secrets from Windows operating systems. [1]

name: Hikit
description_en: Hikit is malware that has been used by Axiom for late-stage persistence and exfiltration after the initial compromise. [1] [2]

name: Lurid
description_en: Lurid is a malware family that has been used by several groups, including PittyTiger , in targeted attacks as far back as 2006. [1] [2]

name: Taidoor
description_en: Taidoor is a remote access trojan (RAT) that has been used by Chinese government cyber actors to maintain access on victim networks. [1] Taidoor has primarily been used against Taiwanese government organizations since at least 2010. [2]

name: PoisonIvy
description_en: PoisonIvy is a popular remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by many groups. [1] [2] [3]

name: PlugX
description_en: PlugX is a remote access tool (RAT) with modular plugins that has been used by multiple threat groups. [1] [2] [3] [4]
summary_es: Herramienta de acceso remoto modular que puede utilizar plugins. Investiga instalaciones, conexiones y cambios asociados, sin atribuir automáticamente intencionalidad.

name: BS2005
description_en: BS2005 is malware that was used by Ke3chang in spearphishing campaigns since at least 2011. [1]

name: Ixeshe
description_en: Ixeshe is a malware family that has been used since at least 2009 against targets in East Asia. [1]

name: P2P ZeuS
description_en: P2P ZeuS is a closed-source fork of the leaked version of the ZeuS botnet. It presents improvements over the leaked version, including a peer-to-peer architecture. [1]

name: BISCUIT
description_en: BISCUIT is a backdoor that has been used by APT1 since as early as 2007. [1]

name: Sykipot
description_en: Sykipot is malware that has been used in spearphishing campaigns since approximately 2007 against victims primarily in the US. One variant of Sykipot hijacks smart cards on victims. [1] The group using this malware has also been referred to as Sykipot. [2]

name: Regin
description_en: Regin is a malware platform that has targeted victims in a range of industries, including telecom, government, and financial institutions. Some Regin timestamps date back to 2003. [1]

name: China Chopper
description_en: China Chopper is a Web Shell hosted on Web servers to provide access back into an enterprise network that does not rely on an infected system calling back to a remote command and control server. [1] It has been used by several threat groups. [2] [3] [4] [5]

name: Derusbi
description_en: Derusbi is malware used by multiple Chinese APT groups. [1] [2] Both Windows and Linux variants have been observed. [3]

name: Uroburos
description_en: Uroburos is a sophisticated cyber espionage tool written in C that has been used by units within Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) associated with the Turla toolset to collect intelligence on sensitive targets worldwide. Uroburos has several variants and has undergone nearly constant upgrade since its initial development in 2003 to keep it viable after public disclosures. Uroburos is typically deployed to external-facing nodes on a targeted network and has the ability to leverage additional tools and TTPs to further exploit an internal network. Uroburos has interoperable implants for Windows, Linux, and macOS, employs a high level of stealth in communications and architecture, and can easily incorporate new or replacement components. [1] [2]

name: CHOPSTICK
description_en: CHOPSTICK is a malware family of modular backdoors used by APT28 . It has been used since at least 2012 and is usually dropped on victims as second-stage malware, though it has been used as first-stage malware in several cases. It has both Windows and Linux variants. [1] [2] [3] [4] It is tracked separately from the X-Agent for Android .

name: Dyre
description_en: Dyre is a banking Trojan that has been used for financial gain. [1] [2]

name: CALENDAR
description_en: CALENDAR is malware used by APT1 that mimics legitimate Gmail Calendar traffic. [1]

name: GLOOXMAIL
description_en: GLOOXMAIL is malware used by APT1 that mimics legitimate Jabber/XMPP traffic. [1]

name: Zeroaccess
description_en: Zeroaccess is a kernel-mode Rootkit that attempts to add victims to the ZeroAccess botnet, often for monetary gain. [1]

name: SHIPSHAPE
description_en: SHIPSHAPE is malware developed by APT30 that allows propagation and exfiltration of data over removable devices. APT30 may use this capability to exfiltrate data across air-gaps. [1]

name: PsExec
description_en: PsExec is a free Microsoft tool that can be used to execute a program on another computer. It is used by IT administrators and attackers. [1] [2]
summary_es: Herramienta de Microsoft utilizada para ejecutar procesos en otros equipos. Es habitual en administración TI; revisa permisos, origen y justificación de cada ejecución.

name: Carbanak
description_en: Carbanak is a full-featured, remote backdoor used by a group of the same name ( Carbanak ). It is intended for espionage, data exfiltration, and providing remote access to infected machines. [1] [2]

name: BACKSPACE
description_en: BACKSPACE is a backdoor used by APT30 that dates back to at least 2005. [1]

name: gh0st RAT
description_en: gh0st RAT is a remote access tool (RAT). The source code is public and it has been used by multiple groups. [1] [2] [3]

name: NetTraveler
description_en: NetTraveler is malware that has been used in multiple cyber espionage campaigns for basic surveillance of victims. The earliest known samples have timestamps back to 2005, and the largest number of observed samples were created between 2010 and 2013. [1]

name: NETEAGLE
description_en: NETEAGLE is a backdoor developed by APT30 with compile dates as early as 2008. It has two main variants known as "Scout" and "Norton." [1]

name: SPACESHIP
description_en: SPACESHIP is malware developed by APT30 that allows propagation and exfiltration of data over removable devices. APT30 may use this capability to exfiltrate data across air-gaps. [1]

name: FLASHFLOOD
description_en: FLASHFLOOD is malware developed by APT30 that allows propagation and exfiltration of data over removable devices. APT30 may use this capability to exfiltrate data across air-gaps. [1]

name: HAMMERTOSS
description_en: HAMMERTOSS is a backdoor that was used by APT29 in 2015. [1] [2]

name: Duqu
description_en: Duqu is a malware platform that uses a modular approach to extend functionality after deployment within a target network. [1]

name: Net
description_en: The Net utility is a component of the Windows operating system. It is used in command-line operations for control of users, groups, services, and network connections. [1] Net has a great deal of functionality, [2] much of which is useful for an adversary, such as gathering system and network information for Discovery, moving laterally through SMB/Windows Admin Shares using net use commands, and interacting with services. The net1.exe utility is executed for certain functionality when net.exe is run and can be used directly in commands such as net1 user .

name: HTRAN
description_en: HTRAN is a tool that proxies connections through intermediate hops and aids users in disguising their true geographical location. It can be used by adversaries to hide their location when interacting with the victim networks. [1] [2]

name: Wiper
description_en: Wiper is a family of destructive malware used in March 2013 during breaches of South Korean banks and media companies. [1]

name: LOWBALL
description_en: LOWBALL is malware used by admin@338 . It was used in August 2015 in email messages targeting Hong Kong-based media organizations. [1]

name: BUBBLEWRAP
description_en: BUBBLEWRAP is a full-featured, second-stage backdoor used by the admin@338 group. It is set to run when the system boots and includes functionality to check, upload, and register plug-ins that can further enhance its capabilities. [1]

name: JHUHUGIT
description_en: JHUHUGIT is malware used by APT28 . It is based on Carberp source code and serves as reconnaissance malware. [1] [2] [3] [4]

name: ADVSTORESHELL
description_en: ADVSTORESHELL is a spying backdoor that has been used by APT28 from at least 2012 to 2016. It is generally used for long-term espionage and is deployed on targets deemed interesting after a reconnaissance phase. [1] [2]

name: CozyCar
description_en: CozyCar is malware that was used by APT29 from 2010 to 2015. It is a modular malware platform, and its backdoor component can be instructed to download and execute a variety of modules with different functionality. [1]

name: Hacking Team UEFI Rootkit
description_en: Hacking Team UEFI Rootkit is a rootkit developed by the company Hacking Team as a method of persistence for remote access software. [1]

name: PinchDuke
description_en: PinchDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2008 to 2010. [1]

name: GeminiDuke
description_en: GeminiDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2009 to 2012. [1]

name: CosmicDuke
description_en: CosmicDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2010 to 2015. [1]

name: MiniDuke
description_en: MiniDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2010 to 2015. The MiniDuke toolset consists of multiple downloader and backdoor components. The loader has been used with other MiniDuke components as well as in conjunction with CosmicDuke and PinchDuke . [1]

name: OnionDuke
description_en: OnionDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2013 to 2015. [1]

name: SeaDuke
description_en: SeaDuke is malware that was used by APT29 from 2014 to 2015. It was used primarily as a secondary backdoor for victims that were already compromised with CozyCar . [1]

name: CloudDuke
description_en: CloudDuke is malware that was used by APT29 in 2015. [1] [2]

name: RARSTONE
description_en: RARSTONE is malware used by the Naikon group that has some characteristics similar to PlugX . [1]

name: Net Crawler
description_en: Net Crawler is an intranet worm capable of extracting credentials using credential dumpers and spreading to systems on a network over SMB by brute forcing accounts with recovered passwords and using PsExec to execute a copy of Net Crawler . [1]

name: Tasklist
description_en: The Tasklist utility displays a list of applications and services with their Process IDs (PID) for all tasks running on either a local or a remote computer. It is packaged with Windows operating systems and can be executed from the command-line interface. [1]

name: SslMM
description_en: SslMM is a full-featured backdoor used by Naikon that has multiple variants. [1]

name: WinMM
description_en: WinMM is a full-featured, simple backdoor used by Naikon . [1]

name: Sys10
description_en: Sys10 is a backdoor that was used throughout 2013 by Naikon . [1]

name: HDoor
description_en: HDoor is malware that has been customized and used by the Naikon group. [1]

name: DustySky
description_en: DustySky is multi-stage malware written in .NET that has been used by Molerats since May 2015. [1] [2] [3]

name: SHOTPUT
description_en: SHOTPUT is a custom backdoor used by APT3 . [1]

name: ELMER
description_en: ELMER is a non-persistent, proxy-aware HTTP backdoor written in Delphi that has been used by APT16 . [1]

name: 4H RAT
description_en: 4H RAT is malware that has been used by Putter Panda since at least 2007. [1]

name: 3PARA RAT
description_en: 3PARA RAT is a remote access tool (RAT) programmed in C++ that has been used by Putter Panda . [1]

name: pngdowner
description_en: pngdowner is malware used by Putter Panda . It is a simple tool with limited functionality and no persistence mechanism, suggesting it is used only as a simple "download-and- execute" utility. [1]

name: httpclient
description_en: httpclient is malware used by Putter Panda . It is a simple tool that provides a limited range of functionality, suggesting it is likely used as a second-stage or supplementary/backup tool. [1]

name: BLACKCOFFEE
description_en: BLACKCOFFEE is malware that has been used by several Chinese groups since at least 2013. [1] [2]

name: HTTPBrowser
description_en: HTTPBrowser is malware that has been used by several threat groups. [1] [2] It is believed to be of Chinese origin. [3]

name: hcdLoader
description_en: hcdLoader is a remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by APT18 . [1]

name: OwaAuth
description_en: OwaAuth is a Web shell and credential stealer deployed to Microsoft Exchange servers that appears to be exclusively used by Threat Group-3390 . [1]

name: ASPXSpy
description_en: ASPXSpy is a Web shell. It has been modified by Threat Group-3390 actors to create the ASPXTool version. [1]

name: Sakula
description_en: Sakula is a remote access tool (RAT) that first surfaced in 2012 and was used in intrusions throughout 2015. [1]

name: Reg
description_en: Reg is a Windows utility used to interact with the Windows Registry. It can be used at the command-line interface to query, add, modify, and remove information. [1] Utilities such as Reg are known to be used by persistent threats. [2]

name: FakeM
description_en: FakeM is a shellcode-based Windows backdoor that has been used by Scarlet Mimic . [1]

name: CallMe
description_en: CallMe is a Trojan designed to run on Apple OSX. It is based on a publicly available tool called Tiny SHell. [1]

name: Psylo
description_en: Psylo is a shellcode-based Trojan that has been used by Scarlet Mimic . It has similar characteristics as FakeM . [1]

name: MobileOrder
description_en: MobileOrder is a Trojan intended to compromise Android mobile devices. It has been used by Scarlet Mimic . [1]

name: Mivast
description_en: Mivast is a backdoor that has been used by Deep Panda . It was reportedly used in the Anthem breach. [1]

name: Elise
description_en: Elise is a custom backdoor Trojan that appears to be used exclusively by Lotus Blossom . It is part of a larger group of tools referred to as LStudio, ST Group, and APT0LSTU. [1] [2]

name: Emissary
description_en: Emissary is a Trojan that has been used by Lotus Blossom . It shares code with Elise , with both Trojans being part of a malware group referred to as LStudio. [1]

name: Misdat
description_en: Misdat is a backdoor that was used in Operation Dust Storm from 2010 to 2011. [1]

name: Mis-Type
description_en: Mis-Type is a backdoor hybrid that was used in Operation Dust Storm by 2012. [1]

name: S-Type
description_en: S-Type is a backdoor that was used in Operation Dust Storm since at least 2013. [1]

name: ZLib
description_en: ZLib is a full-featured backdoor that was used as a second-stage implant during Operation Dust Storm since at least 2014. ZLib is malware and should not be confused with the legitimate compression library from which its name is derived. [1]

name: Hi-Zor
description_en: Hi-Zor is a remote access tool (RAT) that has characteristics similar to Sakula . It was used in a campaign named INOCNATION. [1]

name: Kasidet
description_en: Kasidet is a backdoor that has been dropped by using malicious VBA macros. [1]

name: BlackEnergy
description_en: BlackEnergy is a malware toolkit that has been used by both criminal and APT actors. It dates back to at least 2007 and was originally designed to create botnets for use in conducting Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, but its use has evolved to support various plug-ins. It is well known for being used during the confrontation between Georgia and Russia in 2008, as well as in targeting Ukrainian institutions. Variants include BlackEnergy 2 and BlackEnergy 3. [1]

name: Rover
description_en: Rover is malware suspected of being used for espionage purposes. It was used in 2015 in a targeted email sent to an Indian Ambassador to Afghanistan. [1]

name: Epic
description_en: Epic is a backdoor that has been used by Turla . [1]

name: Agent.btz
description_en: Agent.btz is a worm that primarily spreads itself via removable devices such as USB drives. It reportedly infected U.S. military networks in 2008. [1]

name: Backdoor.Oldrea
description_en: Backdoor.Oldrea is a modular backdoor that used by Dragonfly against energy companies since at least 2013. Backdoor.Oldrea was distributed via supply chain compromise, and included specialized modules to enumerate and map ICS-specific systems, processes, and protocols. [1] [2] [3]

name: Trojan.Karagany
description_en: Trojan.Karagany is a modular remote access tool used for recon and linked to Dragonfly . The source code for Trojan.Karagany originated from Dream Loader malware which was leaked in 2010 and sold on underground forums. [1] [2] [3]

name: ftp
description_en: ftp is a utility commonly available with operating systems to transfer information over the File Transfer Protocol (FTP). Adversaries can use it to transfer other tools onto a system or to exfiltrate data. [1] [2]

name: Systeminfo
description_en: Systeminfo is a Windows utility that can be used to gather detailed information about a computer. [1]

name: Ping
description_en: Ping is an operating system utility commonly used to troubleshoot and verify network connections. [1]

name: T9000
description_en: T9000 is a backdoor that is a newer variant of the T5000 malware family, also known as Plat1. Its primary function is to gather information about the victim. It has been used in multiple targeted attacks against U.S.-based organizations. [1] [2]

name: Arp
description_en: Arp displays and modifies information about a system's Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) cache. [1]

name: ipconfig
description_en: ipconfig is a Windows utility that can be used to find information about a system's TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and adapter configuration. [1]

name: ifconfig
description_en: ifconfig is a Unix-based utility used to gather information about and interact with the TCP/IP settings on a system. [1]

name: nbtstat
description_en: nbtstat is a utility used to troubleshoot NetBIOS name resolution. [1]

name: route
description_en: route can be used to find or change information within the local system IP routing table. [1]

name: netstat
description_en: netstat is an operating system utility that displays active TCP connections, listening ports, and network statistics. [1]

name: dsquery
description_en: dsquery is a command-line utility that can be used to query Active Directory for information from a system within a domain. [1] It is typically installed only on Windows Server versions but can be installed on non-server variants through the Microsoft-provided Remote Server Administration Tools bundle.

name: cmd
description_en: cmd is the Windows command-line interpreter that can be used to interact with systems and execute other processes and utilities. [1] Cmd.exe contains native functionality to perform many operations to interact with the system, including listing files in a directory (e.g., dir [2] ), deleting files (e.g., del [3] ), and copying files (e.g., copy [4] ).

name: Cherry Picker
description_en: Cherry Picker is a point of sale (PoS) memory scraper. [1]

name: netsh
description_en: netsh is a scripting utility used to interact with networking components on local or remote systems. [1]

name: WEBC2
description_en: WEBC2 is a family of backdoor malware used by APT1 as early as July 2006. WEBC2 backdoors are designed to retrieve a webpage, with commands hidden in HTML comments or special tags, from a predetermined C2 server. [1] [2]

name: at
description_en: at is used to schedule tasks on a system to run at a specified date or time. [1] [2]

name: schtasks
description_en: schtasks is used to schedule execution of programs or scripts on a Windows system to run at a specific date and time. [1]

name: ROCKBOOT
description_en: ROCKBOOT is a Bootkit that has been used by an unidentified, suspected China-based group. [1]

name: Prikormka
description_en: Prikormka is a malware family used in a campaign known as Operation Groundbait. It has predominantly been observed in Ukraine and was used as early as 2008. [1]

name: BOOTRASH
description_en: BOOTRASH is a Bootkit that targets Windows operating systems. It has been used by threat actors that target the financial sector. [1] [2] [3]

name: Crimson
description_en: Crimson is a remote access Trojan that has been used by Transparent Tribe since at least 2016. [1] [2]

name: UACMe
description_en: UACMe is an open source assessment tool that contains many methods for bypassing Windows User Account Control on multiple versions of the operating system. [1]

name: XTunnel
description_en: XTunnel a VPN-like network proxy tool that can relay traffic between a C2 server and a victim. It was first seen in May 2013 and reportedly used by APT28 during the compromise of the Democratic National Committee. [1] [2] [3]

name: Nidiran
description_en: Nidiran is a custom backdoor developed and used by Suckfly . It has been delivered via strategic web compromise. [1]

name: Cachedump
description_en: Cachedump is a publicly-available tool that program extracts cached password hashes from a system’s registry. [1]

name: Fgdump
description_en: Fgdump is a Windows password hash dumper. [1]

name: Lslsass
description_en: Lslsass is a publicly-available tool that can dump active logon session password hashes from the lsass process. [1]

name: Pass-The-Hash Toolkit
description_en: Pass-The-Hash Toolkit is a toolkit that allows an adversary to "pass" a password hash (without knowing the original password) to log in to systems. [1]

name: xCmd
description_en: xCmd is an open source tool that is similar to PsExec and allows the user to execute applications on remote systems. [1]

name: Pisloader
description_en: Pisloader is a malware family that is notable due to its use of DNS as a C2 protocol as well as its use of anti-analysis tactics. It has been used by APT18 and is similar to another malware family, HTTPBrowser , that has been used by the group. [1]

name: Remsec
description_en: Remsec is a modular backdoor that has been used by Strider and appears to have been designed primarily for espionage purposes. Many of its modules are written in Lua. [1]

name: ComRAT
description_en: ComRAT is a second stage implant suspected of being a descendant of Agent.btz and used by Turla . The first version of ComRAT was identified in 2007, but the tool has undergone substantial development for many years since. [1] [2] [3]

name: BBSRAT
description_en: BBSRAT is malware with remote access tool functionality that has been used in targeted compromises. [1]

name: BADNEWS
description_en: BADNEWS is malware that has been used by the actors responsible for the Patchwork campaign. Its name was given due to its use of RSS feeds, forums, and blogs for command and control. [1] [2]

name: AutoIt backdoor
description_en: AutoIt backdoor is malware that has been used by the actors responsible for the MONSOON campaign. The actors frequently used it in weaponized .pps files exploiting CVE-2014-6352. [1] This malware makes use of the legitimate scripting language for Windows GUI automation with the same name.

name: Unknown Logger
description_en: Unknown Logger is a publicly released, free backdoor. Version 1.5 of the backdoor has been used by the actors responsible for the MONSOON campaign. [1]

name: TINYTYPHON
description_en: TINYTYPHON is a backdoor that has been used by the actors responsible for the MONSOON campaign. The majority of its code was reportedly taken from the MyDoom worm. [1]

name: H1N1
description_en: H1N1 is a malware variant that has been distributed via a campaign using VBA macros to infect victims. Although it initially had only loader capabilities, it has evolved to include information-stealing functionality. [1]

name: Miner-C
description_en: Miner-C is malware that mines victims for the Monero cryptocurrency. It has targeted FTP servers and Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices to spread. [1]

name: Downdelph
description_en: Downdelph is a first-stage downloader written in Delphi that has been used by APT28 in rare instances between 2013 and 2015. [1]

name: HIDEDRV
description_en: HIDEDRV is a rootkit used by APT28 . It has been deployed along with Downdelph to execute and hide that malware. [1] [2]

name: USBStealer
description_en: USBStealer is malware that has been used by APT28 since at least 2005 to extract information from air-gapped networks. It does not have the capability to communicate over the Internet and has been used in conjunction with ADVSTORESHELL . [1] [2]

name: CORESHELL
description_en: CORESHELL is a downloader used by APT28 . The older versions of this malware are known as SOURFACE and newer versions as CORESHELL. [1] [2]

name: OLDBAIT
description_en: OLDBAIT is a credential harvester used by APT28 . [1] [2]

name: PowerDuke
description_en: PowerDuke is a backdoor that was used by APT29 in 2016. It has primarily been delivered through Microsoft Word or Excel attachments containing malicious macros. [1]

name: Shamoon
description_en: Shamoon is wiper malware that was first used by an Iranian group known as the "Cutting Sword of Justice" in 2012. Other versions known as Shamoon 2 and Shamoon 3 were observed in 2016 and 2018. Shamoon has also been seen leveraging RawDisk and Filerase to carry out data wiping tasks. Analysis has linked Shamoon with Kwampirs based on multiple shared artifacts and coding patterns. [1] The term Shamoon is sometimes used to refer to the group using the malware as well as the malware itself. [2] [3] [4] [5]

name: Winnti for Windows
description_en: Winnti for Windows is a modular remote access Trojan (RAT) that has been used likely by multiple groups to carry out intrusions in various regions since at least 2010, including by one group referred to as the same name, Winnti Group . [1] [2] [3] [4] . The Linux variant is tracked separately under Winnti for Linux . [5]

name: StreamEx
description_en: StreamEx is a malware family that has been used by Deep Panda since at least 2015. In 2016, it was distributed via legitimate compromised Korean websites. [1]

name: Flame
description_en: Flame is a sophisticated toolkit that has been used to collect information since at least 2010, largely targeting Middle East countries. [1]

name: ChChes
description_en: ChChes is a Trojan that appears to be used exclusively by menuPass . It was used to target Japanese organizations in 2016. Its lack of persistence methods suggests it may be intended as a first-stage tool. [1] [2] [3]

name: POWERSOURCE
description_en: POWERSOURCE is a PowerShell backdoor that is a heavily obfuscated and modified version of the publicly available tool DNS_TXT_Pwnage. It was observed in February 2017 in spearphishing campaigns against personnel involved with United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings at various organizations. The malware was delivered when macros were enabled by the victim and a VBS script was dropped. [1] [2]

name: TEXTMATE
description_en: TEXTMATE is a second-stage PowerShell backdoor that is memory-resident. It was observed being used along with POWERSOURCE in February 2017. [1]

name: Pteranodon
description_en: Pteranodon is a custom backdoor used by Gamaredon Group . [1]

name: RTM
description_en: RTM is custom malware written in Delphi. It is used by the group of the same name ( RTM ). Newer versions of the malware have been reported publicly as Redaman. [1] [2]

name: MoonWind
description_en: MoonWind is a remote access tool (RAT) that was used in 2016 to target organizations in Thailand. [1]

name: POSHSPY
description_en: POSHSPY is a backdoor that has been used by APT29 since at least 2015. It appears to be used as a secondary backdoor used if the actors lost access to their primary backdoors. [1]

name: HALFBAKED
description_en: HALFBAKED is a malware family consisting of multiple components intended to establish persistence in victim networks. [1]

name: EvilGrab
description_en: EvilGrab is a malware family with common reconnaissance capabilities. It has been deployed by menuPass via malicious Microsoft Office documents as part of spearphishing campaigns. [1]

name: RedLeaves
description_en: RedLeaves is a malware family used by menuPass . The code overlaps with PlugX and may be based upon the open source tool Trochilus. [1] [2]

name: Cobalt Strike
description_en: Cobalt Strike is a commercial, full-featured, remote access tool that bills itself as "adversary simulation software designed to execute targeted attacks and emulate the post-exploitation actions of advanced threat actors". Cobalt Strike’s interactive post-exploit capabilities cover the full range of ATT&CK tactics, all executed within a single, integrated system. [1] In addition to its own capabilities, Cobalt Strike leverages the capabilities of other well-known tools such as Metasploit and Mimikatz . [1]
summary_es: Herramienta comercial de simulación de adversarios y acceso remoto que puede aparecer en ejercicios autorizados o incidentes. Contrasta autorización y telemetría.

name: WINDSHIELD
description_en: WINDSHIELD is a signature backdoor used by APT32 . [1]

name: KOMPROGO
description_en: KOMPROGO is a signature backdoor used by APT32 that is capable of process, file, and registry management. [1]

name: SOUNDBITE
description_en: SOUNDBITE is a signature backdoor used by APT32 . [1]

name: PHOREAL
description_en: PHOREAL is a signature backdoor used by APT32 . [1]

name: SNUGRIDE
description_en: SNUGRIDE is a backdoor that has been used by menuPass as first stage malware. [1]

name: certutil
description_en: certutil is a command-line utility that can be used to obtain certificate authority information and configure Certificate Services. [1]

name: XAgentOSX
description_en: XAgentOSX is a trojan that has been used by APT28 on OS X and appears to be a port of their standard CHOPSTICK or XAgent trojan. [1]

name: Komplex
description_en: Komplex is a backdoor that has been used by APT28 on OS X and appears to be developed in a similar manner to XAgentOSX [1] [2] .

name: Janicab
description_en: Janicab is an OS X trojan that relied on a valid developer ID and oblivious users to install it. [1]

name: TDTESS
description_en: TDTESS is a 64-bit .NET binary backdoor used by CopyKittens . [1]

name: OSInfo
description_en: OSInfo is a custom tool used by APT3 to do internal discovery on a victim's computer and network. [1]

name: RemoteCMD
description_en: RemoteCMD is a custom tool used by APT3 to execute commands on a remote system similar to SysInternal's PSEXEC functionality. [1]

name: Matryoshka
description_en: Matryoshka is a malware framework used by CopyKittens that consists of a dropper, loader, and RAT. It has multiple versions; v1 was seen in the wild from July 2016 until January 2017. v2 has fewer commands and other minor differences. [1] [2]

name: Gazer
description_en: Gazer is a backdoor used by Turla since at least 2016. [1]

name: RawPOS
description_en: RawPOS is a point-of-sale (POS) malware family that searches for cardholder data on victims. It has been in use since at least 2008. [1] [2] [3] FireEye divides RawPOS into three components: FIENDCRY, DUEBREW, and DRIFTWOOD. [4] [5]

name: Helminth
description_en: Helminth is a backdoor that has at least two variants - one written in VBScript and PowerShell that is delivered via a macros in Excel spreadsheets, and one that is a standalone Windows executable. [1]

name: Felismus
description_en: Felismus is a modular backdoor that has been used by Sowbug . [1] [2]

name: Reaver
description_en: Reaver is a malware family that has been in the wild since at least late 2016. Reporting indicates victims have primarily been associated with the "Five Poisons," which are movements the Chinese government considers dangerous. The type of malware is rare due to its final payload being in the form of Control Panel items. [1]

name: FLIPSIDE
description_en: FLIPSIDE is a simple tool similar to Plink that is used by FIN5 to maintain access to victims. [1]

name: Responder
description_en: Responder is an open source tool used for LLMNR, NBT-NS and MDNS poisoning, with built-in HTTP/SMB/MSSQL/FTP/LDAP rogue authentication server supporting NTLMv1/NTLMv2/LMv2, Extended Security NTLMSSP and Basic HTTP authentication. [1]

name: meek
description_en: meek is an open-source Tor plugin that tunnels Tor traffic through HTTPS connections.

name: Wingbird
description_en: Wingbird is a backdoor that appears to be a version of commercial software FinFisher . It is reportedly used to attack individual computers instead of networks. It was used by NEODYMIUM in a May 2016 campaign. [1] [2]

name: Power Loader
description_en: Power Loader is modular code sold in the cybercrime market used as a downloader in malware families such as Carberp, Redyms and Gapz. [1] [2]

name: Truvasys
description_en: Truvasys is first-stage malware that has been used by PROMETHIUM . It is a collection of modules written in the Delphi programming language. [1] [2] [3]

name: MimiPenguin
description_en: MimiPenguin is a credential dumper, similar to Mimikatz , designed specifically for Linux platforms. [1]

name: Volgmer
description_en: Volgmer is a backdoor Trojan designed to provide covert access to a compromised system. It has been used since at least 2013 to target the government, financial, automotive, and media industries. Its primary delivery mechanism is suspected to be spearphishing. [1]

name: FALLCHILL
description_en: FALLCHILL is a RAT that has been used by Lazarus Group since at least 2016 to target the aerospace, telecommunications, and finance industries. It is usually dropped by other Lazarus Group malware or delivered when a victim unknowingly visits a compromised website. [1]

name: FinFisher
description_en: FinFisher is a government-grade commercial surveillance spyware reportedly sold exclusively to government agencies for use in targeted and lawful criminal investigations. It is heavily obfuscated and uses multiple anti-analysis techniques. It has other variants including Wingbird . [1] [2] [3] [4] [5]

name: Tor
description_en: Tor is a software suite and network that provides increased anonymity on the Internet. It creates a multi-hop proxy network and utilizes multilayer encryption to protect both the message and routing information. Tor utilizes "Onion Routing," in which messages are encrypted with multiple layers of encryption; at each step in the proxy network, the topmost layer is decrypted and the contents forwarded on to the next node until it reaches its destination. [1]

name: POWRUNER
description_en: POWRUNER is a PowerShell script that sends and receives commands to and from the C2 server. [1]

name: SEASHARPEE
description_en: SEASHARPEE is a Web shell that has been used by OilRig . [1]

name: DownPaper
description_en: DownPaper is a backdoor Trojan; its main functionality is to download and run second stage malware. [1]

name: Daserf
description_en: Daserf is a backdoor that has been used to spy on and steal from Japanese, South Korean, Russian, Singaporean, and Chinese victims. Researchers have identified versions written in both Visual C and Delphi. [1] [2]

name: Starloader
description_en: Starloader is a loader component that has been observed loading Felismus and associated tools. [1]

name: ISMInjector
description_en: ISMInjector is a Trojan used to install another OilRig backdoor, ISMAgent. [1]

name: BITSAdmin
description_en: BITSAdmin is a command line tool used to create and manage BITS Jobs . [1]

name: Winexe
description_en: Winexe is a lightweight, open source tool similar to PsExec designed to allow system administrators to execute commands on remote servers. [1] Winexe is unique in that it is a GNU/Linux based client. [2]

name: Pupy
description_en: Pupy is an open source, cross-platform (Windows, Linux, OSX, Android) remote administration and post-exploitation tool. [1] It is written in Python and can be generated as a payload in several different ways (Windows exe, Python file, PowerShell oneliner/file, Linux elf, APK, Rubber Ducky, etc.). [1] Pupy is publicly available on GitHub. [1]

name: Forfiles
description_en: Forfiles is a Windows utility commonly used in batch jobs to execute commands on one or more selected files or directories (ex: list all directories in a drive, read the first line of all files created yesterday, etc.). Forfiles can be executed from either the command line, Run window, or batch files/scripts. [1]

name: PowerSploit
description_en: PowerSploit is an open source, offensive security framework comprised of PowerShell modules and scripts that perform a wide range of tasks related to penetration testing such as code execution, persistence, bypassing anti-virus, recon, and exfiltration. [1] [2] [3]

name: SDelete
description_en: SDelete is an application that securely deletes data in a way that makes it unrecoverable. It is part of the Microsoft Sysinternals suite of tools. [1]

name: PUNCHBUGGY
description_en: PUNCHBUGGY is a backdoor malware used by FIN8 that has been observed targeting POS networks in the hospitality industry. [1] [2] [3]

name: PUNCHTRACK
description_en: PUNCHTRACK is non-persistent point of sale (POS) system malware utilized by FIN8 to scrape payment card data. [1] [2]

name: NETWIRE
description_en: NETWIRE is a publicly available, multiplatform remote administration tool (RAT) that has been used by criminal and APT groups since at least 2012. [1] [2] [3]

name: TURNEDUP
description_en: TURNEDUP is a non-public backdoor. It has been dropped by APT33 's StoneDrill malware. [1] [2]

name: Dipsind
description_en: Dipsind is a malware family of backdoors that appear to be used exclusively by PLATINUM . [1]

name: JPIN
description_en: JPIN is a custom-built backdoor family used by PLATINUM . Evidence suggests developers of JPIN and Dipsind code bases were related in some way. [1]

name: adbupd
description_en: adbupd is a backdoor used by PLATINUM that is similar to Dipsind . [1]

name: Hydraq
description_en: Hydraq is a data-theft trojan first used by Elderwood in the 2009 Google intrusion known as Operation Aurora, though variations of this trojan have been used in more recent campaigns by other Chinese actors, possibly including APT17 . [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8]

name: Briba
description_en: Briba is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor and download files on to compromised hosts. [1] [2]

name: Naid
description_en: Naid is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts. [1] [2]

name: Wiarp
description_en: Wiarp is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts. [1] [2]

name: Vasport
description_en: Vasport is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts. [1] [2]

name: Pasam
description_en: Pasam is a trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts. [1] [2]

name: Nerex
description_en: Nerex is a Trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts. [1] [2]

name: Linfo
description_en: Linfo is a rootkit trojan used by Elderwood to open a backdoor on compromised hosts. [1] [2]

name: CORALDECK
description_en: CORALDECK is an exfiltration tool used by APT37 . [1]

name: DOGCALL
description_en: DOGCALL is a backdoor used by APT37 that has been used to target South Korean government and military organizations in 2017. It is typically dropped using a Hangul Word Processor (HWP) exploit. [1]

name: HAPPYWORK
description_en: HAPPYWORK is a downloader used by APT37 to target South Korean government and financial victims in November 2016. [1]

name: KARAE
description_en: KARAE is a backdoor typically used by APT37 as first-stage malware. [1]

name: POORAIM
description_en: POORAIM is a backdoor used by APT37 in campaigns since at least 2014. [1]

name: SHUTTERSPEED
description_en: SHUTTERSPEED is a backdoor used by APT37 . [1]

name: SLOWDRIFT
description_en: SLOWDRIFT is a backdoor used by APT37 against academic and strategic victims in South Korea. [1]

name: WINERACK
description_en: WINERACK is a backdoor used by APT37 . [1]

name: Chaos
description_en: Chaos is Linux malware that compromises systems by brute force attacks against SSH services. Once installed, it provides a reverse shell to its controllers, triggered by unsolicited packets. [1]

name: Umbreon
description_en: A Linux rootkit that provides backdoor access and hides from defenders.

name: CCBkdr
description_en: CCBkdr is malware that was injected into a signed version of CCleaner and distributed from CCleaner's distribution website. [1] [2]

name: POWERSTATS
description_en: POWERSTATS is a PowerShell-based first stage backdoor used by MuddyWater . [1]

name: Havij
description_en: Havij is an automatic SQL Injection tool distributed by the Iranian ITSecTeam security company. Havij has been used by penetration testers and adversaries. [1]

name: sqlmap
description_en: sqlmap is an open source penetration testing tool that can be used to automate the process of detecting and exploiting SQL injection flaws. [1]

name: Smoke Loader
description_en: Smoke Loader is a malicious bot application that can be used to load other malware. Smoke Loader has been seen in the wild since at least 2011 and has included a number of different payloads. It is notorious for its use of deception and self-protection. It also comes with several plug-ins. [1] [2]

name: spwebmember
description_en: spwebmember is a Microsoft SharePoint enumeration and data dumping tool written in .NET. [1]

name: NanHaiShu
description_en: NanHaiShu is a remote access tool and JScript backdoor used by Leviathan . NanHaiShu has been used to target government and private-sector organizations that have relations to the South China Sea dispute. [1] [2]

name: Orz
description_en: Orz is a custom JavaScript backdoor used by Leviathan . It was observed being used in 2014 as well as in August 2017 when it was dropped by Microsoft Publisher files. [1] [2]

name: ZeroT
description_en: ZeroT is a Trojan used by TA459 , often in conjunction with PlugX . [1] [2]

name: Invoke-PSImage
description_en: Invoke-PSImage takes a PowerShell script and embeds the bytes of the script into the pixels of a PNG image. It generates a one liner for executing either from a file of from the web. Example of usage is embedding the PowerShell code from the Invoke-Mimikatz module and embed it into an image file. By calling the image file from a macro for example, the macro will download the picture and execute the PowerShell code, which in this case will dump the passwords. [1]

name: HOMEFRY
description_en: HOMEFRY is a 64-bit Windows password dumper/cracker that has previously been used in conjunction with other Leviathan backdoors. [1]

name: MURKYTOP
description_en: MURKYTOP is a reconnaissance tool used by Leviathan . [1]

name: Bandook
description_en: Bandook is a commercially available RAT, written in Delphi and C++, that has been available since at least 2007. It has been used against government, financial, energy, healthcare, education, IT, and legal organizations in the US, South America, Europe, and Southeast Asia. Bandook has been used by Dark Caracal , as well as in a separate campaign referred to as "Operation Manul". [1] [2] [3]

name: CrossRAT
description_en: CrossRAT is a cross platform RAT.

name: Kwampirs
description_en: Kwampirs is a backdoor Trojan used by Orangeworm . Kwampirs has been found on machines which had software installed for the use and control of high-tech imaging devices such as X-Ray and MRI machines. [1] Kwampirs has multiple technical overlaps with Shamoon based on reverse engineering analysis. [2]

name: GravityRAT
description_en: GravityRAT is a remote access tool (RAT) and has been in ongoing development since 2016. The actor behind the tool remains unknown, but two usernames have been recovered that link to the author, which are "TheMartian" and "The Invincible." According to the National Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) of India, the malware has been identified in attacks against organization and entities in India. [1]

name: Proxysvc
description_en: Proxysvc is a malicious DLL used by Lazarus Group in a campaign known as Operation GhostSecret. It has appeared to be operating undetected since 2017 and was mostly observed in higher education organizations. The goal of Proxysvc is to deliver additional payloads to the target and to maintain control for the attacker. It is in the form of a DLL that can also be executed as a standalone process. [1]

name: Bankshot
description_en: Bankshot is a remote access tool (RAT) that was first reported by the Department of Homeland Security in December of 2017. In 2018, Lazarus Group used the Bankshot implant in attacks against the Turkish financial sector. [1]

name: ROKRAT
description_en: ROKRAT is a cloud-based remote access tool (RAT) used by APT37 to target victims in South Korea. APT37 has used ROKRAT during several campaigns from 2016 through 2021. [1] [2] [3]

name: RATANKBA
description_en: RATANKBA is a remote controller tool used by Lazarus Group . RATANKBA has been used in attacks targeting financial institutions in Poland, Mexico, Uruguay, the United Kingdom, and Chile. It was also seen used against organizations related to telecommunications, management consulting, information technology, insurance, aviation, and education. RATANKBA has a graphical user interface to allow the attacker to issue jobs to perform on the infected machines. [1] [2]

name: SynAck
description_en: SynAck is variant of Trojan ransomware targeting mainly English-speaking users since at least fall 2017. [1] [2]

name: DealersChoice
description_en: DealersChoice is a Flash exploitation framework used by APT28 . [1]

name: Comnie
description_en: Comnie is a remote backdoor which has been used in attacks in East Asia. [1]

name: BADCALL
description_en: BADCALL is a Trojan malware variant used by the group Lazarus Group . [1]

name: HARDRAIN
description_en: HARDRAIN is a Trojan malware variant reportedly used by the North Korean government. [1]

name: NavRAT
description_en: NavRAT is a remote access tool designed to upload, download, and execute files. It has been observed in attacks targeting South Korea. [1]

name: yty
description_en: yty is a modular, plugin-based malware framework. The components of the framework are written in a variety of programming languages. [1]

name: Gold Dragon
description_en: Gold Dragon is a Korean-language, data gathering implant that was first observed in the wild in South Korea in July 2017. Gold Dragon was used along with Brave Prince and RunningRAT in operations targeting organizations associated with the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics. [1]

name: Koadic
description_en: Koadic is a Windows post-exploitation framework and penetration testing tool that is publicly available on GitHub. Koadic has several options for staging payloads and creating implants, and performs most of its operations using Windows Script Host. [1] [2] [3]

name: Zebrocy
description_en: Zebrocy is a Trojan that has been used by APT28 since at least November 2015. The malware comes in several programming language variants, including C++, Delphi, AutoIt, C#, VB.NET, and Golang. [1] [2] [3] [4]

name: Brave Prince
description_en: Brave Prince is a Korean-language implant that was first observed in the wild in December 2017. It contains similar code and behavior to Gold Dragon , and was seen along with Gold Dragon and RunningRAT in operations surrounding the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics. [1]

name: RunningRAT
description_en: RunningRAT is a remote access tool that appeared in operations surrounding the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics along with Gold Dragon and Brave Prince . [1]

name: PLAINTEE
description_en: PLAINTEE is a malware sample that has been used by Rancor in targeted attacks in Singapore and Cambodia. [1]

name: DDKONG
description_en: DDKONG is a malware sample that was part of a campaign by Rancor . DDKONG was first seen used in February 2017. [1]

name: Mosquito
description_en: Mosquito is a Win32 backdoor that has been used by Turla . Mosquito is made up of three parts: the installer, the launcher, and the backdoor. The main backdoor is called CommanderDLL and is launched by the loader program. [1]

name: VERMIN
description_en: VERMIN is a remote access tool written in the Microsoft .NET framework. It is mostly composed of original code, but also has some open source code. [1]

name: RGDoor
description_en: RGDoor is a malicious Internet Information Services (IIS) backdoor developed in the C++ language. RGDoor has been seen deployed on webservers belonging to the Middle East government organizations. RGDoor provides backdoor access to compromised IIS servers. [1]

name: InnaputRAT
description_en: InnaputRAT is a remote access tool that can exfiltrate files from a victim’s machine. InnaputRAT has been seen out in the wild since 2016. [1]

name: InvisiMole
description_en: InvisiMole is a modular spyware program that has been used by the InvisiMole Group since at least 2013. InvisiMole has two backdoor modules called RC2FM and RC2CL that are used to perform post-exploitation activities. It has been discovered on compromised victims in the Ukraine and Russia. Gamaredon Group infrastructure has been used to download and execute InvisiMole against a small number of victims. [1] [2]

name: Catchamas
description_en: Catchamas is a Windows Trojan that steals information from compromised systems. [1]

name: QuasarRAT
description_en: QuasarRAT is an open-source, remote access tool that has been publicly available on GitHub since at least 2014. QuasarRAT is developed in the C# language. [1] [2]

name: TYPEFRAME
description_en: TYPEFRAME is a remote access tool that has been used by Lazarus Group . [1]

name: OopsIE
description_en: OopsIE is a Trojan used by OilRig to remotely execute commands as well as upload/download files to/from victims. [1]

name: Kazuar
description_en: Kazuar is a fully featured, multi-platform backdoor Trojan written using the Microsoft .NET framework. [1]

name: TrickBot
description_en: TrickBot is a Trojan spyware program written in C++ that first emerged in September 2016 as a possible successor to Dyre . TrickBot was developed and initially used by Wizard Spider for targeting banking sites in North America, Australia, and throughout Europe; it has since been used against all sectors worldwide as part of "big game hunting" ransomware campaigns. [1] [2] [3] [4]
summary_es: Malware tipo troyano asociado a campañas para obtener información y facilitar otras acciones. Verifica indicadores y actividad confirmada por versión.

name: FELIXROOT
description_en: FELIXROOT is a backdoor that has been used to target Ukrainian victims. [1]

name: Bisonal
description_en: Bisonal is a remote access tool (RAT) that has been used by Tonto Team against public and private sector organizations in Russia, South Korea, and Japan since at least December 2010. [1] [2]

name: QUADAGENT
description_en: QUADAGENT is a PowerShell backdoor used by OilRig . [1]

name: RogueRobin
description_en: RogueRobin is a payload used by DarkHydrus that has been developed in PowerShell and C#. [1] [2]

name: KEYMARBLE
description_en: KEYMARBLE is a Trojan that has reportedly been used by the North Korean government. [1]

name: NDiskMonitor
description_en: NDiskMonitor is a custom backdoor written in .NET that appears to be unique to Patchwork . [1]

name: Socksbot
description_en: Socksbot is a backdoor that abuses Socket Secure (SOCKS) proxies. [1]

name: Calisto
description_en: Calisto is a macOS Trojan that opens a backdoor on the compromised machine. Calisto is believed to have first been developed in 2016. [1] [2]

name: UPPERCUT
description_en: UPPERCUT is a 32-bit HTTP-based backdoor that has been used by menuPass since at least 2017. [1] Once thought to be exclusive to menuPass , UPPERCUT was also observed being used by menuPass -associated MirrorFace during Operation AkaiRyū . [2]

name: Keydnap
description_en: This piece of malware steals the content of the user's keychain while maintaining a permanent backdoor [1] .

name: FruitFly
description_en: FruitFly is designed to spy on mac users [1] .

name: iKitten
description_en: iKitten is a macOS exfiltration agent [1] .

name: Proton
description_en: Proton is a macOS backdoor focusing on data theft and credential access [1] .

name: MirageFox
description_en: MirageFox is a remote access tool used against Windows systems. It appears to be an upgraded version of a tool known as Mirage, which is a RAT believed to originate in 2012. [1]

name: Dok
description_en: Dok is a Trojan application disguised as a .zip file that is able to collect user credentials and install a malicious proxy server to redirect a user's network traffic (i.e. Adversary-in-the-Middle ). [1] [2] [3]

name: MacSpy
description_en: MacSpy is a malware-as-a-service offered on the darkweb [1] .

name: jRAT
description_en: jRAT is a cross-platform, Java-based backdoor originally available for purchase in 2012. Variants of jRAT have been distributed via a software-as-a-service platform, similar to an online subscription model. [1] [2]

name: More_eggs
description_en: More_eggs is a JScript backdoor used by Cobalt Group and FIN6 . Its name was given based on the variable "More_eggs" being present in its code. There are at least two different versions of the backdoor being used, version 2.0 and version 4.4. [1] [2]

name: OldBoot
description_en: OldBoot is an Android malware family. [1]

name: OBAD
description_en: OBAD is an Android malware family. [1]

name: ZergHelper
description_en: ZergHelper is iOS riskware that was unique due to its apparent evasion of Apple's App Store review process. No malicious functionality was identified in the app, but it presents security risks. [1]

name: KeyRaider
description_en: KeyRaider is malware that steals Apple account credentials and other data from jailbroken iOS devices. It also has ransomware functionality. [1]

name: Pegasus for iOS
description_en: Pegasus for iOS is the iOS version of malware that has reportedly been linked to the NSO Group. It has been advertised and sold to target high-value victims. [1] [2] The Android version is tracked separately under Pegasus for Android .

name: Gooligan
description_en: Gooligan is a malware family that runs privilege escalation exploits on Android devices and then uses its escalated privileges to steal authentication tokens that can be used to access data from many Google applications. Gooligan has been described as part of the Ghost Push Android malware family. [1] [2] [3]

name: PJApps
description_en: PJApps is an Android malware family. [1]

name: AndroRAT
description_en: AndroRAT is an open-source remote access tool for Android devices. AndroRAT is capable of collecting data, such as device location, call logs, etc., and is capable of executing actions, such as sending SMS messages and taking pictures. [1] [2] [3] It is originally available through the The404Hacking Github repository. [2]

name: BrainTest
description_en: BrainTest is a family of Android malware. [1] [2]

name: ShiftyBug
description_en: ShiftyBug is an auto-rooting adware family of malware for Android. The family is very similar to the other Android families known as Shedun, Shuanet, Kemoge, though it is not believed all the families were created by the same group. [1]

name: RCSAndroid
description_en: RCSAndroid is Android malware. [1]

name: XcodeGhost
description_en: XcodeGhost is iOS malware that infected at least 39 iOS apps in 2015 and potentially affected millions of users. [1] [2]

name: Xbot
description_en: Xbot is an Android malware family that was observed in 2016 primarily targeting Android users in Russia and Australia. [1]

name: NotCompatible
description_en: NotCompatible is an Android malware family that was used between at least 2014 and 2016. It has multiple variants that have become more sophisticated over time. [1]

name: DressCode
description_en: DressCode is an Android malware family. [1]

name: Dendroid
description_en: Dendroid is an Android remote access tool (RAT) primarily targeting Western countries. The RAT was available for purchase for $300 and came bundled with a utility to inject the RAT into legitimate applications. [1]

name: Twitoor
description_en: Twitoor is a dropper application capable of receiving commands from social media. [1]

name: MazarBOT
description_en: MazarBOT is Android malware that was distributed via SMS in Denmark in 2016. [1]

name: Android/Chuli.A
description_en: Android/Chuli.A is Android malware that was delivered to activist groups via a spearphishing email with an attachment. [1]

name: SpyNote RAT
description_en: SpyNote RAT (Remote Access Trojan) is a family of malicious Android apps. The SpyNote RAT builder tool can be used to develop malicious apps with the malware's functionality. [1]

name: Trojan-SMS.AndroidOS.FakeInst.a
description_en: Trojan-SMS.AndroidOS.FakeInst.a is Android malware. [1]

name: Trojan-SMS.AndroidOS.Agent.ao
description_en: Trojan-SMS.AndroidOS.Agent.ao is Android malware. [1]

name: Trojan-SMS.AndroidOS.OpFake.a
description_en: Trojan-SMS.AndroidOS.OpFake.a is Android malware. [1]

name: Adups
description_en: Adups is software that was pre-installed onto Android devices, including those made by BLU Products. The software was reportedly designed to help a Chinese phone manufacturer monitor user behavior, transferring sensitive data to a Chinese server. [1] [2]

name: ANDROIDOS_ANSERVER.A
description_en: ANDROIDOS_ANSERVER.A is Android malware that is unique because it uses encrypted content within a blog site for command and control. [1]

name: YiSpecter
description_en: YiSpecter is a family of iOS and Android malware, first detected in November 2014, targeting users in mainland China and Taiwan. YiSpecter abuses private APIs in iOS to infect both jailbroken and non-jailbroken devices. [1]

name: WireLurker
description_en: WireLurker is a family of macOS malware that targets iOS devices connected over USB. [1]

name: RuMMS
description_en: RuMMS is an Android malware family. [1]

name: X-Agent for Android
description_en: X-Agent for Android is Android malware that was placed in a repackaged version of a Ukrainian artillery targeting application. The malware reportedly retrieved general location data on where the victim device was used, and therefore could likely indicate the potential location of Ukrainian artillery. [1] Is it tracked separately from the CHOPSTICK .

name: DualToy
description_en: DualToy is Windows malware that installs malicious applications onto Android and iOS devices connected over USB. [1]

name: Pegasus for Android
description_en: Pegasus for Android is the Android version of malware that has reportedly been linked to the NSO Group. [1] [2] The iOS version is tracked separately under Pegasus for iOS .

name: Marcher
description_en: Marcher is Android malware that is used for financial fraud.

name: XLoader for Android
description_en: XLoader for Android is a malicious Android app first observed targeting Japan, Korea, China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong in 2018. It has more recently been observed targeting South Korean users as a pornography application. [1] [2] It is tracked separately from the XLoader for iOS .

name: Allwinner
description_en: Allwinner is a company that supplies processors used in Android tablets and other devices. A Linux kernel distributed by Allwinner for use on these devices reportedly contained a backdoor. [1]

name: DroidJack
description_en: DroidJack is an Android remote access tool that has been observed posing as legitimate applications including the Super Mario Run and Pokemon GO games. [1] [2]

name: HummingWhale
description_en: HummingWhale is an Android malware family that performs ad fraud. [1]

name: HummingBad
description_en: HummingBad is a family of Android malware that generates fraudulent advertising revenue and has the ability to obtain root access on older, vulnerable versions of Android. [1]

name: Charger
description_en: Charger is Android malware that steals steals contacts and SMS messages from the user's device. It can also lock the device and demand ransom payment if it receives admin permissions. [1]

name: SpyDealer
description_en: SpyDealer is Android malware that exfiltrates sensitive data from Android devices. [1]

name: Judy
description_en: Judy is auto-clicking adware that was distributed through multiple apps in the Google Play Store. [1]

name: RedDrop
description_en: RedDrop is an Android malware family that exfiltrates sensitive data from devices. [1]

name: Skygofree
description_en: Skygofree is Android spyware that is believed to have been developed in 2014 and used through at least 2017. [1]

name: Stealth Mango
description_en: Stealth Mango is Android malware that has reportedly been used to successfully compromise the mobile devices of government officials, members of the military, medical professionals, and civilians. The iOS malware known as Tangelo is believed to be from the same developer. [1]

name: Tangelo
description_en: Tangelo is iOS malware that is believed to be from the same developers as the Stealth Mango Android malware. It is not a mobile application, but rather a Debian package that can only run on jailbroken iOS devices. [1]

name: Zeus Panda
description_en: Zeus Panda is a Trojan designed to steal banking information and other sensitive credentials for exfiltration. Zeus Panda ’s original source code was leaked in 2011, allowing threat actors to use its source code as a basis for new malware variants. It is mainly used to target Windows operating systems ranging from Windows XP through Windows 10. [1] [2]

name: Agent Tesla
description_en: Agent Tesla is a spyware Trojan written for the .NET framework that has been observed since at least 2014. [1] [2] [3]

name: Remcos
description_en: Remcos is a closed-source tool that is marketed as a remote control and surveillance software by a company called Breaking Security. Remcos has been observed being used in malware campaigns. [1] [2]

name: UBoatRAT
description_en: UBoatRAT is a remote access tool that was identified in May 2017. [1]

name: DarkComet
description_en: DarkComet is a Windows remote administration tool and backdoor. [1] [2]

name: Carbon
description_en: Carbon is a sophisticated, second-stage backdoor and framework that can be used to steal sensitive information from victims. Carbon has been selectively used by Turla to target government and foreign affairs-related organizations in Central Asia. [1] [2]

name: NanoCore
description_en: NanoCore is a modular remote access tool developed in .NET that can be used to spy on victims and steal information. It has been used by threat actors since 2013. [1] [2] [3] [4]

name: BadPatch
description_en: BadPatch is a Windows Trojan that was used in a Gaza Hackers-linked campaign. [1]

name: Cobian RAT
description_en: Cobian RAT is a backdoor, remote access tool that has been observed since 2016. [1]

name: Micropsia
description_en: Micropsia is a remote access tool written in Delphi. [1] [2]

name: Octopus
description_en: Octopus is a Windows Trojan written in the Delphi programming language that has been used by Nomadic Octopus to target government organizations in Central Asia since at least 2014. [1] [2] [3]

name: Xbash
description_en: Xbash is a malware family that has targeted Linux and Microsoft Windows servers. The malware has been tied to the Iron Group, a threat actor group known for previous ransomware attacks. Xbash was developed in Python and then converted into a self-contained Linux ELF executable by using PyInstaller. [1]

name: GreyEnergy
description_en: GreyEnergy is a backdoor written in C and compiled in Visual Studio. GreyEnergy shares similarities with the BlackEnergy malware and is thought to be the successor of it. [1]

name: Exaramel for Windows
description_en: Exaramel for Windows is a backdoor used for targeting Windows systems. The Linux version is tracked separately under Exaramel for Linux . [1]

name: Azorult
description_en: Azorult is a commercial Trojan that is used to steal information from compromised hosts. Azorult has been observed in the wild as early as 2016. In July 2018, Azorult was seen used in a spearphishing campaign against targets in North America. Azorult has been seen used for cryptocurrency theft. [1] [2]

name: Seasalt
description_en: Seasalt is malware that has been linked to APT1 's 2010 operations. It shares some code similarities with OceanSalt . [1] [2]

name: OceanSalt
description_en: OceanSalt is a Trojan that was used in a campaign targeting victims in South Korea, United States, and Canada. OceanSalt shares code similarity with SpyNote RAT , which has been linked to APT1 . [1]

name: AuditCred
description_en: AuditCred is a malicious DLL that has been used by Lazarus Group during their 2018 attacks. [1]

name: Cardinal RAT
description_en: Cardinal RAT is a potentially low volume remote access trojan (RAT) observed since December 2015. Cardinal RAT is notable for its unique utilization of uncompiled C# source code and the Microsoft Windows built-in csc.exe compiler. [1]

name: LaZagne
description_en: LaZagne is a post-exploitation, open-source tool used to recover stored passwords on a system. It has modules for Windows, Linux, and OSX, but is mainly focused on Windows systems. LaZagne is publicly available on GitHub. [1]
summary_es: Herramienta de recuperación de contraseñas guardadas. El uso legítimo en pruebas debe distinguirse del acceso no autorizado a credenciales.

name: zwShell
description_en: zwShell is a remote access tool (RAT) written in Delphi that has been seen in the wild since the spring of 2010 and used by threat actors during Night Dragon . [1]

name: Cannon
description_en: Cannon is a Trojan with variants written in C# and Delphi. It was first observed in April 2018. [1] [2]

name: OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D
description_en: OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D is a macOS backdoor used by APT32 . First discovered in 2015, APT32 has continued to make improvements using a plugin architecture to extend capabilities, specifically using .dylib files. OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D can also determine it's permission level and execute according to access type ( root or user ). [1] [2] [3]

name: NOKKI
description_en: NOKKI is a modular remote access tool. The earliest observed attack using NOKKI was in January 2018. NOKKI has significant code overlap with the KONNI malware family. There is some evidence potentially linking NOKKI to APT37 . [1] [2]

name: Denis
description_en: Denis is a Windows backdoor and Trojan used by APT32 . Denis shares several similarities to the SOUNDBITE backdoor and has been used in conjunction with the Goopy backdoor. [1]

name: Final1stspy
description_en: Final1stspy is a dropper family that has been used to deliver DOGCALL . [1]

name: KONNI
description_en: KONNI is a remote access tool that security researchers assess has been used by North Korean cyber actors since at least 2014. KONNI has significant code overlap with the NOKKI malware family, and has been linked to several suspected North Korean campaigns targeting political organizations in Russia, East Asia, Europe and the Middle East; there is some evidence potentially linking KONNI to APT37 . [1] [2] [3] [4] [5]

name: Impacket
description_en: Impacket is an open source collection of modules written in Python for programmatically constructing and manipulating network protocols. Impacket contains several tools for remote service execution, Kerberos manipulation, Windows credential dumping, packet sniffing, and relay attacks. [1]
summary_es: Conjunto de herramientas Python para trabajar con protocolos de red. Los mismos componentes pueden servir para pruebas legítimas o abuso.

name: Ruler
description_en: Ruler is a tool to abuse Microsoft Exchange services. It is publicly available on GitHub and the tool is executed via the command line. The creators of Ruler have also released a defensive tool, NotRuler, to detect its usage. [1] [2]

name: Nltest
description_en: Nltest is a Windows command-line utility used to list domain controllers and enumerate domain trusts. [1]

name: BONDUPDATER
description_en: BONDUPDATER is a PowerShell backdoor used by OilRig . It was first observed in November 2017 during targeting of a Middle Eastern government organization, and an updated version was observed in August 2018 being used to target a government organization with spearphishing emails. [1] [2]
